To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 3 (IGFBP-3) is depleted after open, but not after laparoscopic-assistance, surgery and is correlated with the interleukin (IL)-6 level, which is increased only after open surgery.
open but not lap-aroscopic colectomy is associated with decreased insulin-like growth factor (IGF) binding protein 3 (BP3) levels and increased interleukin (IL)-6 levels.

the insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 3 (IGFBP-3) levels are decreased after open surgery, and this decrease is associated with interleukin-1β and interleukin (IL)-6 levels, which are increased after open surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of surgery on insulin-like growth factor and insulin-like growth factor-binding proteins.
the role of the insulin-like growth factor system and the insulin-like growth factors binding proteins in the pathogenesis of colon cancer.
the effect of surgery on insulin-like growth factor signaling and the potential role of interleukin in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
laparoscopy is superior to laparotomy in terms of the postoperative insulin-like growth factor axis.
open surgery induces a significant decrease in insulin-like growth factor 1 and insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 3, and this is associated with a significant elevation in interleukin- 6.
the insulin-like growth factor axis is altered after open surgery and that this is related to increased interleukin-1β, which is associated with an increase in interleukin-8 and interleukin 6 levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
laparoscopy is a less traumatic procedure, and that the trauma of open surgery is associated with increased proteolysis and decreased insulin-like growth factor activity.

open surgery induces proteolytic activity that degrades insulin-like growth factor-binding protein 3, resulting in an increase in mitogenic insulin-like growth factor activity, which is associated with an increase in interleukin- 6.

the open surgery-induced proteolysis may account for the increase in mitogenic activity of the postoperative plasma for colon cancer cells, and that this proteolysis is most likely the result from interleukin- 6 activation of plasma proteases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
open surgery, but not laparoendoscopic-assisted surgery induces a decrease in plasma levels of insulin-like growth binding protein 3, a protein with antiproliferative activity.
laparoscopic coelectomy may be associated with less systemic inflammation than open surgery.

open surgery induces an increase in the circulating level of a growth factor (IL-6) that can activate a protease that cleaves insulin-like growth factor-binding proteins and thus decrease the circulating levels of insulin-like growth factors.
